Rahul + Kim to schedule infra deep dive and run perf baseline (week of 2027-06-07)
Maya to set up onboarding workspace and invite Larkspur team to Console trial

action_items: Ava Martinez: Send onboarding guide + security pack (due: 2027-06-03)
Rahul Gupta: Schedule infra deep dive and attach baseline checklist (due: 2027-06-06)

summary: Kickoff for Redwood onboarding with Larkspur Health. Discussed goals (pilot latency and cost targets, data residency, SSO), high-level timeline, initial technical requirements (VPC, KMS, audit logs), and next steps to run performance baseline and share security docs. Agreed to schedule infra deep dive next week.
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. This is Ava from Redwood, I’m the AE, with Rahul our solutions engineer and Maya our CSM. How’s everyone doing?
[00:08] Jared Thompson: Good, thanks. Excited to get going, I think we sent a couple emails but wanted to get aligned on the kickoff.
[00:14] Priya Patel: Yep, Priya here. We want to validate latency and cost for our triage assistant use case across roughly 10k daily active users.
[00:22] Ava Martinez: Great. Quick agenda — goals, timeline, infra requirements, security, and next steps. Does that sound ok?
[00:29] Kim Rivera: Works for me. We’re also scoped on data residency — some PHI-ish data we want to avoid sending to hosted unless encrypted and logged.
[00:36] Maya Chen: Noted, Kim. We’ve onboarded similar customers with either Dedicated or Private setups depending on their compliance needs. We’ll map options.
[00:44] [01:05] Rahul Gupta: On the tech side, I want to understand your request pattern — average sequence lengths, concurrency, and whether you need streaming. That drives kernel selection and batching heuristics.
[01:16] Priya Patel: Average prompt ~150 tokens, responses ~120 tokens. Peak concurrency maybe 40 qps, steady 10–15.
[01:25] Rahul Gupta: Ok that’s super helpful. For 40 qps peaks, we may recommend a small Dedicated pool for the pilot to keep latency predictable; hosted could work but with some variability.
[01:36] Jared Thompson: Cost is a factor though — we don’t have budget for heavy reserved infra yet. Could we start hosted and move to Dedicated if SLA shows need?
[01:45] Ava Martinez: Absolutely, that’s common. Redwood supports staged approach — start hosted to get going, run baselines, then move to Dedicated with pinned model versions. We can show cost comparisons.
[01:56] [05:02] Kim Rivera: Network question — we do prefer VPC peering or PrivateLink. Does Redwood support VPC endpoints and customer-managed KMS?
[05:11] Maya Chen: Yes, for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS (HSM options) and support VPC peering. For Dedicated, there are private network options and audit logs.
[05:22] Kim Rivera: Cool, I’ll pull our network diagram and share.
[05:27] [07:10] Rahul Gupta: For the performance baseline, we’ll need a sample prompt set and representative concurrency. We’ll also run token breakdowns so you can see unit costs per prompt.
[07:20] Priya Patel: We can share a sanitized set — remove PII — but include the different instruction styles.
[07:26] Rahul Gupta: Perfect. Also, which model family are you evaluating? Any preference for quantized variants?
[07:32] Priya Patel: We tried a few open models; performance vs cost tradeoff matters. We’re open to Redwood recommendations — maybe a 7B quantized variant if quality holds.
[07:42] Rahul Gupta: Sounds good. For our defaults, we’ll propose 7B quantized and one 13B float for comparison during the baseline.
[07:51] [12:00] Jared Thompson: On security, we need SOC2 + encryption at rest and in transit, audit logs, and SSO for user access. Also want to know data retention policies.
[12:12] Maya Chen: Redwood has SOC2 and can provide the security pack. We support SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM provisioning. Data retention is configurable; we can set short retention during pilot and provide audit log exports.
[12:28] Priya Patel: Do you have any customers with EHR-adjacent data? Curious how private deployments are handled.
[12:36] Maya Chen: Yes, a few — typically they choose Private or Dedicated with strict KMS and VPC. We can share anonymized architecture diagrams.
[12:45] [18:04] Kim Rivera: From our infra side, we need to confirm IP ranges, firewall rules, and whether there’s dependency on accepting a managed VPC.
[18:12] Rahul Gupta: We’ll provide a network checklist. For Dedicated we do allow static egress IPs and dedicated endpoints.
[18:20] Kim Rivera: Good to know. Also, how are model rollouts handled? We want canary testing and easy rollback.
[18:28] Ava Martinez: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. We’ll demo that in the technical deep dive.
[18:36] [24:00] Jared Thompson: Timeline — we’re hoping to start pilot within 3 weeks if onboarding goes smoothly. Is that realistic?
[24:07] Maya Chen: Yes, typical pilot can be 2–4 weeks. First week for infra/setup and SSO, second for baseline, third for tuning.
[24:15] Ava Martinez: Actionable: we’ll send the onboarding guide and security docs today. Rahul will run perf baselines once we have prompt sets and network access.
[24:25] Priya Patel: We can provide sanitized prompt set by end of day tomorrow.
[24:30] [30:10] Rahul Gupta: Quick note — for latency targets under 300ms 95th, we’ll likely need batching tuned carefully and possibly Dedicated. I’ll outline batching configurations and expected tradeoffs.
[30:22] Priya Patel: 300ms 95th is our aspirational target. If you can show evidence in baseline that’s great.
[30:29] Rahul Gupta: Will do. We’ll include token-level latency breakdowns.
[30:35] [36:05] Kim Rivera: On compliance, we’ll need the SOC2 report and details on key management. Also, can you confirm that audit logs include token-level request metadata?
[36:13] Maya Chen: Yes, we can export request-level logs and correlate to tokens. KMS integration details are in the security pack.
[36:22] Kim Rivera: Ok I’ll add that to action items.
[36:28] [42:00] Ava Martinez: Recap — Larkspur aims to validate performance and cost for the triage assistant, prefer private connectivity, need SOC2 and KMS details, pilot target ~3 weeks. Next steps — Ava sends docs, Rahul + Kim to schedule infra deep dive, Maya to create trial workspace.
[42:20] Jared Thompson: Sounds good. Also please include an estimated budget comparison between starting hosted vs small Dedicated pool.
[42:29] Ava Martinez: Yes we’ll include a short cost model for the expected qps and token sizes.
[42:36] Priya Patel: One last question — for model version pinning, can we freeze the model for rollouts?
[42:41] Rahul Gupta: Yes, you can pin model versions and route requests; rollouts are controlled in the Console.
[42:48] [48:55] Maya Chen: I’ll send calendar invites for the infra deep dive and the Console walkthrough. Expect invites by tomorrow.
[49:03] Kim Rivera: Thanks everyone.
[49:06] Jared Thompson: Thanks, appreciate it.
[49:10] Ava Martinez: Thanks all — talk soon.
[49:15] [END]
